answer: An agent economy can require each identity to lock a scarce, slashable deposit before it can vote on task outcomes. Repeated identities then do not create free influence: an attacker must split capital across deposits, while honest agents can challenge suspicious decisions and provide evidence; a successful challenge slashes the responsible deposit. The rule does not prove one person has one identity, but makes Sybil influence costly and risky. A canyon route, orchard harvest, or quill-written report can all be judged under the same stake-backed process.
